problems.title: Universal zero-shot superiority is false
claim: NuCLR exceeds every baseline in all zero-shot tasks.
analysis: Current Table 1 reports inductive zero-shot Bugeon E/I macro F1 \(0.6738\pm0.0563\) for NuCLR and \(0.7463\pm0.0095\) for LOLCAT. The mean difference is \(-0.0725\), or \(-7.25\) percentage points. The same page still says NuCLR consistently outperforms all baselines in zero-shot settings. LOLCAT uses a different training paradigm, but is explicitly included in that comparison. This refutes the universal wording while preserving the other reported wins; these aggregates alone do not support a new significance calculation.
result: The bounded local discrepancy or counterexample is supported; no change in published benchmark scores is quantified.

problems.title: Development does not fully hold out the target animal
problems.source_location: Current paper, hyperparameter search Section B.4, p. 19, and Bugeon Section D.4, pp. 21–22; author configs/data/val_dataset/bugeon_val_dev.yaml and configs/data/bugeon_inductive.yaml.
claim: Development and testing completely separate the target animal.
analysis: The current development configuration includes SB028 recording sb028_20191106, while inductive testing includes sb028_20191107, sb028_20191108, sb028_20191112 and sb028_20191113. Final pretraining explicitly excludes all five. Thus recording sets are disjoint but model-development and test animals are not completely disjoint. Section B.4 says calcium-imaging hyperparameters were tuned on the Bugeon development set, and D.4 discloses one development recording from every subject. This limits a fully untouched-animal interpretation; it does not contradict the narrower final-pretraining exclusion or establish test-label supervised fitting or a quantified F1 bias.
result: This is a scope/provenance gap, not proof that the stronger empirical conclusion is false.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Reconcile the specific equation, reported quantity or source contract described above. Corrected full-experiment results remain unverified.

problems.title: IBL counts and split ratios differ
problems.source_location: Current paper, Section D.2, p. 21; author IBL training/development/test YAMLs and preprocess/ibl_bwm/create_transductive_splits.py, lines 59–70.
claim: Public configurations reproduce the reported IBL counts and split ratios.
analysis: The current text reports total/train-development/development/test recording counts \((439,346,91,93)\). Removing probe suffixes from the current released YAML identifiers gives \((455,362,90,93)\). The development records are included in pretraining, while pretraining and final-test record IDs remain disjoint. A larger metadata universe is not itself an error; the inclusion/version mapping is missing. The split script reserves \(20\%\) for testing and then \(1/8\) of the remainder for validation, giving \(70/10/20\%\) train/validation/test, whereas reserving \(20\%\) of the training fold as described gives \(64/16/20\%\), apart from integer rounding. Historical production settings are not established by current code alone.

problems.title: Current uncertainty labels distinguish seed SD from figure SEM
problems.source_location: Current paper, Table 1, p. 7; Table 2, p. 8; Figure 3, p. 15; current arXiv revision omits the older conference checklist.
claim: The current tables and figure identify their uncertainty summaries.
analysis: The current tables explicitly use standard deviations across training seeds, while Figure 3 explicitly uses standard error across three seeds. Different summaries in distinct identified displays are compatible. The older conference checklist claimed SEM throughout, but that checklist is absent from this current arXiv revision. For \(n\) independent seeds, \(\mathrm{SEM}=\mathrm{SD}/\sqrt n\); neither quantity estimates animal-sampling uncertainty. The single held-out Bugeon animal and three held-out Steinmetz animals still bound the scope of population-level generalization.
result: The older contradictory checklist statement is not a current-source error. Seed variability and animal-level uncertainty remain different quantities; no numerical error is inferred from using clearly labeled summaries.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: The current revision removes the conflicting checklist and labels each reported summary; the remaining point concerns inferential scope.
problems.existing_correction_status: The conflicting older checklist is absent from the current revision; no claim of author adoption of this review is made.
